title: Permanent red team: product state, authorization, consent, queue, outage, resource exhaustion

waveGRoleSeparation.note: Migration 0018 is NOT in the RC baseline; it was applied into a throwaway schema only to attack it.

method.stack: Real local stack: Fastify API built in-process against real PostgreSQL 16.15 (localhost:5433/pickle_test), real migrations + seed + published scoring release, real media-worker deletion pipeline, fake object store and in-memory queue where the local stack has no S3/SQS.
method.isolation: Every new attack suite creates its own PostgreSQL schema, runs migrations, and drops the schema afterwards. No held-out case was touched (wm-dink-01, afn-vic-rally1 untouched).
method.scope: New attacks only. Explicitly NOT re-counted as new: wave-D12/E19 Result and Try Again state work, wave-F f26 fabricated-provenance Result defects, wave-F f21 bounded scheduler red team, capture-envelope/OOD bypasses (f22/D3-07), previously reported consent-abuse cases, and external Mac/iPhone blockers.
method.unit: One attack case = one distinct adversarial request sequence or SQL privilege probe. Frames are not counted as trials.
method.gates: pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm format:check all pass on this branch. DB-backed suites re-run with DATABASE_URL_TEST set. Mobile: npx tsc --noEmit + npm test.

by_category.category: auth/authorization abuse (IDOR, forged claims, cross-tenant writes)
malformed request/protocol (path ids, bodies, content types, oversize)
DB privilege bypass vs wave-g role separation (0018)
by_category.detail: 10 probes DENIED by role separation (session_replication_role, UPDATE consent_record, sequence ALTER/setval, LOCK TABLE, SET ROLE x2, COPY TO PROGRAM, pg_read_file, CREATE EXTENSION); 7 ALLOWED (forged-pseudonym append, de-pseudonymizing join x2 incl. readonly role, readonly identity read, TEMP TABLE, app_user DELETE cascade, tombstone read).

by_category.category: permission failure sequences (privacy toggle, consent withdrawal)

measured_results.counts: 500/500 open practice sessions accepted for one account, 0 rejections, 935-972 ms total (~1.9 ms/session). GET /v1/progress with that backlog: 200 in 9 ms. GET /v1/library/sessions?limit=100: 200 in 5 ms; limit=200 rejected with a typed 400.
measured_results.conclusion: No latency collapse, but no per-account cap and no application-level rate limiting exist.

measured_results.counts: shots:sync with 201 shots -> 400 validation.shots_sync (contract cap 200). One shot carrying 2000 duplicate 'contact' phase spans -> 200 accepted, 1 shot_phase row persisted (UNIQUE (shot_id, phase_key) dedupes). 2 MiB body -> 413 validation.payload_too_large.

measured_results.measurement: datastore outage injection (API pointed at a dead port)
measured_results.counts: Before fix: 3/3 authenticated routes returned 500 api.internal_error kind=permanent retryable=false. After fix: 3/3 return 503 api.datastore_unavailable kind=retryable retryable=true; /v1/health still 200.

Redelivered and concurrent media.purge: master + derived objects deleted exactly once, later redeliveries report no object to delete. Duplicate final_hard_delete rows: before fix both rows stayed queued indefinitely; after fix both converge. Duplicate terminal tasks stay queued (correctly) while an object-store purge is genuinely outstanding.

measured_results.measurement: test suite results after all fixes
measured_results.counts: services/api 107/107 passed (with DATABASE_URL_TEST); services/media-worker 29/29 passed; apps/mobile 41 suites / 400 tests passed; root pnpm test 593 passed + 4 skipped across 51 files in swing-lab plus all other workspaces green; typecheck, lint, format:check clean.

fixed.title: Cross-user analysis attachment: any authenticated user could bind an analysis to another user's session
fixed.root_cause: POST /v1/analyses accepted body.sessionId without verifying the session belonged to the caller.
fixed.fix: Ownership lookup on practice_session before association; unowned ids answer 404 session.not_found.

fixed.title: Forged admin: any token carrying pickle_role=admin obtained full admin API access
fixed.root_cause: requireAdmin trusted the token-derived role only; app_user has no role column, so nothing server-side constrained who may claim admin.
fixed.fix: Server-configured ADMIN_AUTH_SUBJECTS allowlist; outside development a token claim alone can no longer grant admin, refusals log and return 403 auth.admin_not_authorized.
fixed.residual_risk: Production MUST set ADMIN_AUTH_SUBJECTS. With it unset in a non-development environment all admin access is refused (fail-closed); with the variable absent in development the legacy permissive behavior remains.

fixed.title: Media upload completed and retained after the user disabled cloud video sync
fixed.root_cause: Privacy setting was checked when the upload was initiated but not at completion, so an opt-out during upload left the asset stored.
fixed.fix: Completion re-checks cloud_sync_enabled, marks the asset deleted, enqueues media.purge, audits media.discarded_cloud_sync_disabled, and returns 403 media.cloud_sync_disabled.

fixed.title: Finalized session summary went stale when a shot synced after finalize
fixed.fix: Shared summary computation extracted to services/api/src/modules/sessions/summary.ts; a late shot refreshes an existing summary and practice_session.avg_score without reopening the session.

fixed.title: Malformed path ids and malformed bodies produced 500 api.internal_error
fixed.fix: preValidation rejects non-UUID path ids with 400 validation.path_id; request-level failures map onto typed 4xx (400/413/415/429) instead of 500.
fixed.regression: 13 path-id routes and 5 body/content-type cases in services/api/test/h27.redteam.integration.test.ts

fixed.title: TRY AGAIN handoff never expired: an abandoned declaration re-armed an unrelated later capture (measured with a 6-hour-old handoff)
fixed.fix: 30 s TTL plus clearTryAgainHandoff(); AnalyzeScreen clears a pending handoff when the entry point is not the camera.

fixed.title: Duplicate final_hard_delete deletion tasks blocked each other forever, so account deletion never completed
fixed.fix: Worker pending-work query excludes other final_hard_delete rows.

fixed.title: Datastore outage was reported as a permanent, non-retryable failure, so clients would discard queued work
fixed.fix: Connection-class failures (ECONN*, ETIMEDOUT, PG 08*, 57P0*, 53300/53400, pool timeouts) return 503 api.datastore_unavailable kind=retryable.

fixed.title: Client-supplied consent decision timestamps could be dated arbitrarily far in the future
fixed.fix: Decisions are accepted within 5 minutes of clock skew and rejected beyond it.

unresolved.title: No per-account resource cap and no application- or gateway-level rate limiting
unresolved.evidence: 500 consecutive session creations accepted with zero rejections at ~1.9 ms each; no rate-limit middleware exists anywhere in services/api/src.
unresolved.why_unresolved: Choosing a cap or a rate-limit tier is a product/infrastructure policy decision (edge gateway vs application middleware) and inventing a limit here could break legitimate high-volume sync. Reported rather than silently patched.
unresolved.impact: An authenticated account can grow its own row count without bound; read latency did not degrade at the volumes measured.

unresolved.title: Wave-G role separation does not prevent re-identification of pseudonymous consent subjects
unresolved.evidence: Against migration 0018 in a throwaway schema, both the runtime role and the read-only role could join consent_record to consent_subject and read app_user identifiers (probes R6, R13, R14).
unresolved.why_unresolved: Migration 0018 lives on origin/devin/wave-g/g10-f23-roles, not on the RC baseline; the fix (restricting consent_subject to a dedicated role/schema) belongs to that workstream, and editing it from this branch would collide with wave-g.
unresolved.note: Role separation did hold against 10 other privilege probes, including all consent_record mutation, sequence tampering, SET ROLE escapes, COPY TO PROGRAM, and server file reads.

p2_findings.title: API integration suites drop and recreate the shared public schema, so parallel suite files raced during migrations
p2_findings.fix: services/api/vitest.config.ts sets fileParallelism:false; the DB gate now passes 107/107 deterministically.

p2_findings.title: Runtime DB role can append a consent record for an arbitrary pseudonym (probe R1)
p2_findings.detail: Subject binding is enforced in the API, not in the database; a compromised runtime role could attribute a grant to another subject. History remains append-only: UPDATE/DELETE on consent_record stayed denied.

p2_findings.title: phases/checkpoints arrays in shots:sync are unbounded in the contract
p2_findings.detail: 2000 duplicate phase spans were accepted but only 1 row persisted (DB uniqueness) and the 1 MiB body limit caps amplification, so no bound was added.

p2_findings.title: Consent export v1 is unsigned when no signing key is configured
p2_findings.detail: Observed with the local test configuration (consentExportSigningKey unset). If production requires signed exports this must be enforced by deployment configuration.

rationale: All three P0 breaks found in this gate were reproduced on the real local stack, root-caused, fixed on this branch, and locked with regressions, and 6 of 8 P1 breaks are likewise fixed and covered. The gate still fails for broad release for two reasons that are not internally solvable here: (1) the P0-2 fix is only effective if the deployment sets ADMIN_AUTH_SUBJECTS — an unconfigured non-development deployment fails closed, but the RC as previously shipped would have granted admin to any token bearing a pickle_role=admin claim, so release must confirm the configuration; and (2) no per-account cap or rate limiting exists anywhere in the API (500/500 session creations accepted), which is a policy decision that must be made before broad exposure. The wave-g re-identification finding is additionally owed to that workstream. This gate converts to PASS once ADMIN_AUTH_SUBJECTS is provisioned in the release configuration and a rate-limit/quota decision is implemented at the edge or in the API.
limitations_and_external_blockers: No iPhone, Mac, Swift, or Apple Vision execution was available: no on-device authorization, capture, or latency behavior was attacked or measured, and none is claimed.
No real S3/SQS: object storage and queue attacks used a fake object store and the in-memory queue, plus induced dispatch failures. Real SQS redelivery semantics and IAM policy were not attacked.

Malformed *video* media was not re-attacked: capture-envelope and OOD bypasses are already covered by wave-D3/f22 suites and re-running them would not be a new attack. Malformed media coverage here is protocol-level (bodies, content types, sizes, identifiers).

DB privilege probes ran as the local superuser-owned test cluster user for setup and then as the wave-g runtime/readonly roles; a hardened production cluster (network policy, pgbouncer, IAM auth) was not represented.
Counts are attack cases, not user sessions; no labels, coach reviews, or device measurements were produced or implied by this gate.
